name: graveyard
description: a small, neglected graveyard behind the mansion. crumbling headstones lean at odd angles like broken teeth. a large stone mausoleum stands at the far end, its heavy door slightly ajar, a sliver of darkness within. the air is cold and unnaturally still. no birds sing here. fresh lilies lie at one grave.

items.name: headstone
items.description: a weathered headstone, older than the others: 'eleanor blackwood, 1847-1891. may her soul find peace. forgive us, eleanor.' the date is unusual — she died the same year the family vanished. fresh lilies lie at its base.

items.name: wilting_lilies
items.description: fresh lilies at eleanor's grave. they can't be more than a day old. but no one has been here in 130 years. who left them?

items.name: other_graves
items.description: the other headstones mark the graves of servants and distant relatives. the most recent is dated 1889. one grave catches your eye — a small, simple stone with no name, only a date: 'october 31st, 1891.' the same day the family vanished.

items.name: brass_key
items.description: a small brass key hidden under a loose stone near eleanor's grave. the stone was recently disturbed.

items.name: dirt_path
items.description: the dirt path leading from the garden gate to the mausoleum is well-worn. despite the overgrown garden, this path has been used recently. footprints in the damp earth — a woman's shoes, narrow heels, size six or seven.

items.name: family_plot
items.description: a cluster of smaller headstones bearing the blackwood name. the children: 'thomas, age 12. — elizabeth, age 10. — james, age 8. — margaret, age 6. — eleanor the younger, age 3.' but these graves are empty — they were never buried here. the stones were placed as memorials.

exits.description: a rusty iron gate covered in climbing ivy. it creaks as it swings.
the heavy stone door of the mausoleum, slightly ajar. cold air seeps from the darkness within.
